---
title: "How to upload"
---

Each person has a folder in the repository and uploads one notebook or script per week. The site reads a short header at the top of each file to see which objectives it covers. Nothing is run: your files are only read and shown.

## 1. Create your folder (once)

1. Open the repository on GitHub and go to **Add file → Create new file**.
2. In the name box type `people/yourname/profile.txt`. Typing the slashes creates the folder. Use a nickname if you prefer, since the site is public.
3. In the file, write:

```
name: Your name or nickname
language: Python
```

4. Click **Commit changes**.

## 2. Upload each week

1. Open your folder and choose **Add file → Upload files**.
2. Drag in your Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`), R script (`.R`) or MATLAB script (`.m`).
3. Click **Commit changes**. The site updates a few minutes later.

Uploading a file with the same name replaces the earlier version.

## 3. Add the header

The header lists the objective IDs from the module page. Put it at the very top of the file.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `objectives` | IDs you have covered. These count as **Done** |
| `attempted` | IDs you worked on but did not finish (optional) |
| `week` | Week number within the module (optional) |
| `title` | A short name shown on the site (optional) |

**Notebook:** make the first cell a Raw cell (or a Markdown cell) containing:

```
---
objectives: [2.1, 2.2, 2.3]
attempted: [2.4]
week: 1
---
```

**R script:** start the file with

```
# ---
# objectives: [3.1, 3.2]
# week: 1
# ---
```

**MATLAB script:** start the file with

```
% ---
% objectives: [3.1, 3.2]
% week: 1
% ---
```

An objective is Done once any of your uploads lists it. A file without a header is still shown, but counts for nothing.

## What gets published

The site is public. Everything in your notebook is published, including its outputs. Upload code and small example data only: no personal data and no unpublished results. Clear notebook outputs that show such data before you upload.
